title: Real roads + real hazard evacuation-routing run (Yeongdeok 2025)

origin_scan.note: ignition proxy = centroid of t0 >=0.5 hazard core; reach band does not bind (exceeds graph footprint)

hazard_source.constructed_via: HazardSequence(grid, times_min, surfaces) — direct, not from_forward_sim

provenance.statement: BOTH road topology AND fire-hazard surface are REAL. Roads/refuges are real OpenStreetMap geometry (OSMnx, EPSG:5179); the hazard is the real spread_v2 forward-simulated ignition-probability field for the held-out Yeongdeok 2025 fire. Closes the limitation that road topology and fire-hazard surface were never simultaneously real.
still_synthetic_or_assumed: NO DEM slope correction on the OSM walk edges: edge times use a FLAT elderly walk speed. This is a real methodological difference from the other runs, which build the walk lattice with Tobler slope correction (build_evacuation_network). The OSM nodes carry no attached DEM, so no per-node slope is invented here — walk timing is distance/flat-speed only. Disclosed, not hidden.
elderly-home origins (seeded sampled candidates; real per-household data is private)

consequences: results dominated by the near-static >=0.5 core, not front advance
NOT directly comparable to the ~439-origin rescue run on timing
third cell of the real/synthetic axis table, not a like-for-like replacement

comparison_to_407_run.why_fewer_help_and_far_fewer_trapped: On the REAL OSM walk network with 46 REAL refuge nodes, connectivity and shelter density are far higher than on the synthetic 8-connected lattice used by the 407 run. Consequently FEWER origins need future-aware routing to stay safe (naive_into_FA_safe 18 vs 56) and FAR FEWER are trapped with no safe route (3 vs 88). This is evidence that the synthetic lattice was PESSIMISTIC about real-world evacuability, NOT that the future-aware method is weak — the method's benefit (naive walks into fire, future-aware detours cleanly) still appears on 18 real homes, and the 3 genuinely-trapped homes are real, reported outcomes.

partition_completeness.this_run: 438 + 18 + 3 = 459 EXACTLY; naive_unreachable = 0 and unclassified = 0. Every scanned origin lands in exactly one bucket — the partition is complete and asserted.
partition_completeness.run_407: 56 + 88 + 240 = 384 classified out of 407 scanned — a 23-origin gap (origins that fell outside the then-reported buckets).
partition_completeness.claim: This run's classifier is a methodological improvement: the six-bucket partition (adding naive_unreachable + unclassified as explicit sinks) provably accounts for 100% of scanned origins, closing the 407 run's 23-origin gap.

self_corrected_discrepancy.observed: An intermediate scratch run reported 21 / 3 / 435 (naive_into_FA_safe / no_safe_route / both_safe); the reproducible script reports 18 / 3 / 438.
self_corrected_discrepancy.cause: The intermediate run round-tripped the OSM graph through GraphML and RELABELED nodes to 0..N-1 integers. The stride-18 origin sub-sample is taken over sorted(node_ids), so relabeling changed WHICH 459 origins were sampled — shifting 3 origins between naive_into_FA_safe and both_safe. no_safe_route (3) and the partition total (459) were unaffected.
self_corrected_discrepancy.resolution: The CANONICAL result is the reproducible script's 18 / 3 / 438, which samples over the REAL OSM node ids (matching the repo convention in rescue_demo._scan_origins). scripts/run_real_roads_real_hazard.py regenerates it deterministically. The relabeled 21/3/435 figures are superseded.

method_matches_repo: 6-bucket partition from scripts/run_routing_integration.py; routing via evacuation.naive_route / future_aware_route (unchanged).

future_aware.note: no safe route: hazard envelope overtakes all shelters within budget

git_head_note: git_head = round2-clean HEAD (the base this additive branch is cut from). A live run stamps the branch HEAD at run time.
